clause.text: 1.01. Distribution Right. The distribution right shall be limited to all countries and all of their territories and possessions within the continent known as South America ("Territory") (Exhibit "B" attached hereto). Distributor shall not assign the rights granted in this Section 1.01 without the prior written consent of the Company.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants Distributor an exclusive right to sell the Company’s products in all of South America, which directly conflicts with the playbook position that the agreement must be non‑exclusive. The playbook states: "This Agreement is non-exclusive. Each party remains free to provide to, procure from, or contract with any third party for services of the same or a similar kind, without restriction and without any obligation to the other party." (no-exclusivity) This exclusive dealing commitment is therefore disallowed and creates a high contractual risk.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.

reviews.rationale: The clause provides indemnification for patent infringement but limits the supplier's remedy to either procuring the right to continue using the product or providing a similar product. Because the clause omits these additional remedies, it does not fully comply with the approved fallback provision and leaves the indemnitee exposed to insufficient relief, resulting in a high risk.

6.02. Termination. This Agreement may be terminated only:

(a) By either party for substantial breach of any material provision of this Agreement by the other, provided due notice has been given to the other of the alleged breach and such other party has not cured the breach within (30) days] thereof; or

(b) By the Company if: there is an unacceptable change in the control or management of the Distributor; if the Distributor makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors; if a petition in bankruptcy is filed by or against the Distributor, resulting in an adjudication of bankruptcy; or, if the Distributor fails to pay its debts as they become due and provided due notice has been given by the Company to the Distributor and the Distributor has not cured such breach within thirty (30) days thereof; or (c) By the written consent of both parties;

 (d) Upon termination of this Agreement all further rights and obligations of the parties shall cease, except that Distributor shall not be relieved of (i) its obligation to pay any monies due, or to become due, as of or after the date of termination, and (ii) any other obligation set forth in this Agreement which is to take effect after the date of termination.

reviews.rationale: The clause restricts termination rights to cause and limited company‑only events, omitting the playbook’s preferred termination‑for‑convenience right that allows either party to end the agreement on thirty (30) days' notice. This creates an imbalance and increased risk for the Company, contrary to the playbook position [termination-for-convenience] which mandates a convenience termination provision.
